what_it_does: Searching for the most similar item to a query across a large database — for example, finding the image most like a text description — requires comparing millions of numeric feature vectors, which is slow and burns a lot of memory bandwidth on a conventional processor. MIRACLE targets this problem for multimodal data (data mixing text, images, audio, etc.). It combines two specialized hardware mechanisms: in-memory processing (doing the math inside the memory chip itself rather than shipping data to the processor — here using random hashing to quickly narrow down candidates) and content-addressable memory (a special circuit that searches all its entries in parallel in a single step, rather than reading through them one at a time). A final re-ranking step using the standard cosine similarity measure (which computes how 'aligned' two vectors are) recovers the accuracy that the fast approximate stages traded away.
